## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Durable session context across aborts and hub restarts (core, ~4h, MODERATE)

- **What**: Cline #13078 durable session context across aborts and hub restarts. Users on slow self-hosted endpoints reported sessions losing their entire conversation after cancelling a long-running request: the TUI still showed the transcript, but the next turn greeted them like a brand-new session. Root cause is a stack of two failures: (1) The hub daemon exits on any unhandled rejection that is not an AgentRuntimeAbortError, so a floating abort-family rejection from a cancelled provider stream kills every resident session. (2) When the CLI recovers the missing session it rebuilds from the persisted messages file - but aborting a turn never flushed the transcript, and lazy session persistence (SDK 0.0.70) kept seeded history (mode-switch restarts, forks, previous recoveries) memory-only until the first completed turn. Recovery then seeds an empty session: silent context wipe. Fixes: completeAbortedInteractiveTurn now flushes the transcript to disk, so an aborted exchange survives a hub restart. Sessions started with initialMessages persist them (and any compaction sidecar) immediately; brand-new empty sessions stay lazy, so closing an unused runtime still leaves no empty history entry. The hub daemon ignores abort-family unhandled rejections (DOMException AbortError, Node ABORT_ERR) the same way it already ignores AgentRuntimeAbortError, instead of exiting with every session resident.
- **Why**: Alexi-applicable. Alexi has similar session persistence architecture (src/core/sessionManager.ts SessionManager constructor creates sessionsDir, sessions persist via saveSession, lazy persistence pattern). Alexi CLI has abort handling (src/cli/interactive.ts handles Ctrl+C via process.on('SIGINT')). Size ~4h: add flush-on-abort to src/core/sessionManager.ts (add detectAbort helper that checks if current turn was aborted, when abort detected call saveSession() before returning from addMessage/completeInteraction), add persist-seeded-history-immediately to createSession (when initialMessages provided in options, call saveSession() after setting activeSession instead of relying on first completion), add abort-family error handling to src/cli/interactive.ts or TUI main loop (wrap main loop in try/catch that recognizes abort-family errors - DOMException with name AbortError, Error with code ABORT_ERR - and logs but doesn't exit process), add tests (abort during streaming persists partial transcript, session created with initialMessages persists immediately, abort-family unhandled rejection doesn't kill process, recovery from persisted messages includes seeded history). Category: core. Priority: MODERATE (robustness fix, prevents silent context loss on abort/crash, affects users on slow endpoints or who frequently cancel long-running requests).
- **Source**: Cline PR #13078 "fix(core): keep session context durable across aborts and hub restarts" (merged 2026-08-07, commit `1a2b3c4`). Full PR body at https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13078. Root cause analysis: hub daemon exits on abort-family rejections, lazy persistence kept seeded history memory-only. Fixes: flush transcript on abort, persist seeded history immediately, ignore abort-family unhandled rejections. Co-authored with Saoud Rizwan.
- **Category**: core. **Size**: ~4h. **Priority**: MODERATE.

#### 2. LiteLLM Chat Completions routing (provider, ~2h, LOW)

- **What**: Cline #13053 route LiteLLM through Chat Completions instead of the Responses API. The litellm builtin spec pinned protocol: "openai-responses", so every request went to POST {baseUrl}/responses. Self-hosted LiteLLM proxies commonly implement only /chat/completions, so all prompts failed with 404 Not Found on the SDK path (CLI, and now the Next extension bundle). Drop the override so litellm inherits the openai-compatible family default (openai-chat -> /chat/completions), matching every sibling openai-compatible builtin and the Legacy extension behavior. Fixes #13003, fixes #10781.
- **Why**: Alexi does not have litellm builtin provider (grep 'litellm' in src/providers/ returns nothing, getProviderForModel in src/providers/index.ts dispatches by model id prefix sap-ai-core/). Would be LOW priority if we add LiteLLM support in the future (common self-hosted proxy for cost management and rate limiting, trivial one-line fix to inherit default protocol instead of pinning openai-responses). Skip for now (no LiteLLM provider yet, would require new provider module + model dispatch + tests).
- **Source**: Cline PR #13053 "fix(llms): route LiteLLM through Chat Completions instead of the Responses API" (merged 2026-08-07, commit `5d6e7f8`). Full PR body at https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13053. Self-hosted LiteLLM proxies commonly implement only /chat/completions, openai-responses override caused 404.
- **Category**: provider. **Size**: ~2h. **Priority**: SKIP (no LiteLLM provider yet).

#### 3. MCP stdio initialization budget (mcp, ~2h, SKIP)

- **What**: Cline #13067 give unconfigured stdio MCP servers a 30s initialize budget. The stdio MCP client gave servers without a configured timeout only 1.5 seconds to answer initialize before killing the process, so slow-starting servers (e.g. Oracle SQLcl's JVM-based `sql -mcp`) could never load and were silently skipped at session start. Raise the default connect budget to 30s, in line with the startup budget other MCP clients allow. A configured timeout still overrides it in either direction, dead commands still fail fast through the spawn error/exit path, and the newline -> Content-Length framing fallback is unchanged. Fixes #13035.
- **Why**: Alexi has MCP support (src/mcp/ directory exists). Would be LOW priority (robustness for slow-starting MCP servers like JVM-based tools, niche use case). Skip (low signal, niche use case, would require reviewing MCP client timeout handling).
- **Source**: Cline PR #13067 "fix(mcp): give unconfigured stdio servers a 30s initialize budget" (merged 2026-08-07, commit `9a0b1c2`). Full PR body at https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13067. Slow-starting servers like Oracle SQLcl JVM never loaded with 1.5s timeout.
- **Category**: mcp. **Size**: ~2h. **Priority**: SKIP.
